newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies called mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies called mostly lower.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were called mostly 0.10 to 0.20 cent per lb lower and pork bellies steady to 0.30 cent a lb lower, analysts said.

Lower cash pork prices Tuesday and weak packer demand for hogs Wednesday should weigh on hog futures, sources said. USDA reported pork cutout values late Tuesday were down $0.67 to $0.55 per lb, with much of that decline due to drops in cash loin and rib prices.
In hogs, several meat packers said they bought much of Wednesday's slaughter needs on Tuesday.
Pork belly futures were called mostly lower, largely following live hog futures, analysts and traders said.
Cash belly prices were steady Tuesday at $89.00 per cwt , which some analysts said may be bearish to the futures. They said storage interests should boost cash prices.
However, other traders said the futures do not offer a profitable hedge to store bellies, which may be discouraging buying of fresh bellies for storage.

USDA on May 20 reported there were 54.017 million lbs of frozen pork bellies in storage, down from 54.767 million a month earlier and from 57.174 million a year ago. Analysts said the May figure was only the second time on record that the May supply was less than the April one.
